Why do you still believe it? [1]: They (claim to) take 45% of ad placement sales, so not including revenue from selling trends/user data. mentions.text: Since you're watching on those players, I can guess where you got your media. While eg Netflix will have multiple audio streams, almost all pirate releases don't. So while there does exist a 2.1 stereo mix in the world, you're not going to see it. That's your initial problem. But it's entirely solvable with software. You need a dialogue boost, to fix the missing center channel, as well as a night mode to crush the dynamic range. Or at least one of the two. Your complaint is entirely solvable with simple software. However removing dynamic range is a one way path, and if it's removed then it's impossible to get it back. So then people that do have decent speakers and want a good listening experience can't. It's possible for Blu-ray to include a stereo mix, they can have multiple audio tracks, but realistically most people buying physical media have speakers or at least a soundbar.
